title: Cool Eva — Trouble codes
description: Every diagnostic code the bike has reported, named from Energica's own type-approval table, with the history that makes an intermittent fault visible.

panels.title: Codes active
panels.description: How many codes the Connectivity Hub currently reports as ACTIVE. This is the bike saying what is wrong right now, and it changes minute to minute — P0A07 was seen flipping 0↔1 on a stationary bike on 2026-08-02. Zero here does not mean the fault is gone; check the timeline below.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS value
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
-- no lower bound: log-on-change means the last change can predate the
-- window, and a held value beats "No data", which reads as a dead logger.
WHERE s.key = 'dtc_list_count' AND r.ts <= $__to
ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Codes stored (OBD)
panels.description: OBD-II PID 0x01's stored-fault count — the bike's fault HISTORY, not what is wrong now. Normally far larger than the active count (38 vs 0-1 here) because it accumulates and is only cleared by a scan tool. The two are different measurements down completely different paths and are not meant to agree.

panels.title: Unrecognised codes
panels.description: Codes the bike reported that are NOT in the 148-entry type-approval table. Non-zero means either a code the document omits (components 51, 52 and 60 are absent from it) or that the 20-bit field is being read wrongly. Either way it is worth looking at the raw frames in the journal.

panels.title: Each code, active vs clear
panels.description: The reason this dashboard exists. Every diagnostic code the bike has reported, as a band over time. An intermittent fault — one that latches for a single poll and clears — is invisible on a counter and unmissable here. Rows are written log-on-change, so a band continues until the next change: a long 'active' stripe means it stayed set, not that it was re-reported. Codes are labelled with their OBD number and Energica's own description.

, dtc AS (

  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key LIKE 'dtc\_%\_%' ESCAPE '\'
    AND s.key NOT IN ('dtc_count', 'dtc_list_count', 'dtc_unrecognised_count')
    AND r.ts <= $__to
), seed AS (
  SELECT key, MAX(ts) AS ts FROM dtc WHERE ts < $__from GROUP BY key
), points AS (
  SELECT key, ts, value FROM dtc WHERE ts >= $__from
  UNION ALL
  SELECT d.key, $__from, d.value FROM dtc d JOIN seed ON seed.key = d.key AND seed.ts = d.ts
)
SELECT p.ts/1000.0 AS time,
       COALESCE(c.obd, 'raw ' || SUBSTR(p.key, 5)) || ' — ' || COALESCE(c.descr, 'not in code table') AS metric,
       CASE WHEN p.value > 0 THEN 'active' ELSE 'clear' END AS value
FROM points p
LEFT JOIN code c ON c.key = p.key
ORDER BY p.ts

Ignores the START of the dashboard time range, not the end: it reports every code recorded up to the right edge of the window, so panning back to an old ride shows the fault history as it stood then, matching the timeline above rather than contradicting it.

, edge AS (
  SELECT s.key AS key, r.ts AS ts, r.value AS value,
         LAG(r.value) OVER (PARTITION BY s.key ORDER BY r.ts) AS prev
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key LIKE 'dtc\_%\_%' ESCAPE '\'
    AND s.key NOT IN ('dtc_count', 'dtc_list_count', 'dtc_unrecognised_count')
    AND r.ts <= $__to
)
SELECT COALESCE(c.obd, 'raw ' || SUBSTR(e.key, 5)) AS "Code",
       COALESCE(c.descr, 'not in Energica''s code table') AS "What it means",
       COALESCE(c.name, '') AS "OBD name",
       -- '?' on a LEFT JOIN miss, not 'no': every other column COALESCEs the miss
       -- explicitly, and a confident "the lamp does not light for this" two columns
       -- from "not in Energica's code table" is a claim we cannot make. The phone
       -- view omits the clause entirely in that case; this keeps them agreeing.
       -- A NULL c.mil is that same refusal one level in — the code IS in the
       -- table, but no source states its lamp behaviour, which is true of six of
       -- them. Without this arm `c.mil = 1` is NULL rather than false, so the ELSE
       -- would answer 'no' for exactly the codes the table's null exists to withhold
       -- an answer for. public/views/faults.js prints 'unknown' for the same rows.
       CASE WHEN c.key IS NULL OR c.mil IS NULL THEN '?' WHEN c.mil = 1 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Lights lamp",
       -- Rising edges only. Counting rows would report a code that latched once as
       -- having fired hundreds of times, because the server re-broadcasts whole state.
       SUM(CASE WHEN e.value > 0 AND (e.prev IS NULL OR e.prev <= 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Times set",
       DATETIME(MIN(CASE WHEN e.value > 0 THEN e.ts END)/1000, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS "First seen",
       DATETIME(MAX(CASE WHEN e.value > 0 THEN e.ts END)/1000, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS "Last seen"
FROM edge e
LEFT JOIN code c ON c.key = e.key
GROUP BY e.key
HAVING "Times set" > 0
ORDER BY MAX(CASE WHEN e.value > 0 THEN e.ts END) DESC

, edge AS (
  SELECT s.key AS key, r.ts AS ts, r.value AS value,
         LAG(r.value) OVER (PARTITION BY s.key ORDER BY r.ts) AS prev
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key LIKE 'dtc\_%\_%' ESCAPE '\'
    AND s.key NOT IN ('dtc_count', 'dtc_list_count', 'dtc_unrecognised_count')
    AND r.ts <= $__to
)
SELECT COALESCE(c.obd, 'raw ' || SUBSTR(e.key, 5)) AS "Code",
       COALESCE(c.descr, 'not in Energica''s code table') AS "What it means",
       COALESCE(c.name, '') AS "OBD name",
       -- '?' on a LEFT JOIN miss, not 'no': every other column COALESCEs the miss
       -- explicitly, and a confident "the lamp does not light for this" two columns
       -- from "not in Energica's code table" is a claim we cannot make. The phone
       -- view omits the clause entirely in that case; this keeps them agreeing.
       -- A NULL c.mil is that same refusal one level in — the code IS in the
       -- table, but no source states its lamp behaviour, which is true of six of
       -- them. Without this arm `c.mil = 1` is NULL rather than false, so the ELSE
       -- would answer 'no' for exactly the codes the table's null exists to withhold
       -- an answer for. public/views/faults.js prints 'unknown' for the same rows.
       CASE WHEN c.key IS NULL OR c.mil IS NULL THEN '?' WHEN c.mil = 1 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Lights lamp",
       -- Rising edges only. Counting rows would report a code that latched once as
       -- having fired hundreds of times, because the server re-broadcasts whole state.
       SUM(CASE WHEN e.value > 0 AND (e.prev IS NULL OR e.prev <= 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Times set",
       DATETIME(MIN(CASE WHEN e.value > 0 THEN e.ts END)/1000, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS "First seen",
       DATETIME(MAX(CASE WHEN e.value > 0 THEN e.ts END)/1000, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS "Last seen"
FROM edge e
LEFT JOIN code c ON c.key = e.key
GROUP BY e.key
HAVING "Times set" > 0
ORDER BY MAX(CASE WHEN e.value > 0 THEN e.ts END) DESC

panels.title: The two counts, side by side
panels.description: dtc_count is OBD-II's STORED history; dtc_list_count is the hub's ACTIVE list. They are different measurements and their disagreement is expected, not a bug — confirmed 2026-08-03 when the active list was observed flickering while the stored count sat at 38. A jump in the stored count is a new fault being remembered; a spike in the active count is something happening right now.

WITH counts AS (
  SELECT s.key AS key, r.ts AS ts, r.value AS value
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('dtc_count', 'dtc_list_count', 'dtc_unrecognised_count')
    AND r.ts <= $__to
), edges AS (
  SELECT key, MAX(CASE WHEN ts < $__from THEN ts END) AS before_ts, MAX(ts) AS latest_ts
  FROM counts GROUP BY key
)
SELECT ts/1000.0 AS time, key AS metric, value FROM counts WHERE ts >= $__from
UNION ALL
SELECT $__from/1000.0, c.key, c.value
  FROM counts c JOIN edges e ON e.key = c.key AND e.before_ts = c.ts
UNION ALL
SELECT $__to/1000.0, c.key, c.value
  FROM counts c JOIN edges e ON e.key = c.key AND e.latest_ts = c.ts
ORDER BY time
